Our HistoryHBCC has been bringing organised chess to Hobsons Bay since 1974 and has been affiliated with Chess Victoria since 1975 1974–1977: The Club Begins 1974 HBCC is formed in Altona North Nissen huts at the Altona North Football Club HBCC began when Kevin Brown and Bob Grieves (with early members including John Vranes and John Dunlop) played late into the night in the old football club changing huts — tough winters, huge passion. Hobsons Bay Chess Club Inc. 1974 First Club Champion crowned Geoff Page Geoff Page became the first HBCC club champion — an early marker of the competitive culture forming around the club. Hobsons Bay Chess Club Inc. 1975 Move to Fifth Ave & first chess sets funded A stronger home base in the western suburbs As the sports club established at Fifth Ave, chess became part of the club (“why not chess?”). Max Fry donated $100 to buy sets, helping the club grow. Hobsons Bay Chess Club Inc. 1975 Festival tradition begins Operation Recreation (now Bayside Festival) Bob Grieves and Kevin Brown famously played chess while being towed on a trailer in the street parade — sparking a long-running festival presence and many new members. Hobsons Bay Chess Club Inc. [bold_timeline_item_button title=”Expand” style=”” shape=”” color=”” size=”inline” url=”#” el_class=”bold_timeline_group_button”] 1978–1984: Early Champions & “Best in the West” 1978–1981 A dominant champion era George Cagalj (with a break in 1979) George Cagalj won the club championship three times (1978, 1980, 1981), with John Gedeljovski interrupting the run in 1979. Hobsons Bay Chess Club Inc. 1982–1984 Peter Caissa era Championship hat-trick (shared with Hartmut “Harry” Schultheiss) Peter Caissa took over as champion in 1982–84 (with Harry Schultheiss), reflecting the club’s growing strength and depth. Hobsons Bay Chess Club Inc. 1982 “Best in the West” is launched A flagship tradition begins The inaugural Best in the West Open started a tradition of attracting top local and international players to Melbourne’s west — becoming a major name in Australian chess. Hobsons Bay Chess Club Inc. [bold_timeline_item_button title=”Expand” style=”” shape=”” color=”” size=”inline” url=”#” el_class=”bold_timeline_group_button”] 1985–1994: Big Names & Chess on the Air 1984–1986 Harry Schultheiss takes the title A strong competitive chapter Harry Schultheiss held the club championship through the mid-80s before the next wave of champions emerged. Hobsons Bay Chess Club Inc. 1987–1989 Mario Zoppi returns to dominate A new contender arrives: Stan Christodoulou Mario Zoppi commanded the late 80s. Around this time, Stan Christodoulou (Greek-Egyptian Candidate Master from Switzerland) joined the club. Hobsons Bay Chess Club Inc. 1991 Chess Chat radio program begins First radio chess program in Australia Club leaders helped launch “Chess Chat” on Stereo 974 — a dedicated chess community radio program that reached players across Melbourne via talkback and guests. Hobsons Bay Chess Club Inc. 1994 International recognition Featured in German chess magazine “Europa Rochade” Chess Chat’s impact was recognised internationally when highlighted in “Europa Rochade.” Hobsons Bay Chess Club Inc. [bold_timeline_item_button title=”Expand” style=”” shape=”” color=”” size=”inline” url=”#” el_class=”bold_timeline_group_button”] 1997–2003: New Identity, New Venues 1997 The club becomes a “nomad” After the demise of ANBY Sports Club With ANBY ending, the club moved through a series of venues across Altona and Williamstown — a challenging period of constant relocation. Hobsons Bay Chess Club Inc. 1998 Reborn as Hobsons Bay Chess Club Move to ADASS Centre, Walker Close The committee pushed for stability, and the club adopted the Hobsons Bay Chess Club name, relocating to the ADASS Centre near the club’s earliest origins. Hobsons Bay Chess Club Inc. 2003 Joan Kirner House becomes home A new base in Williamstown In early 2003, the club moved to Joan Kirner House (refurbished former courthouse), continuing the search for the “right” long-term venue. Hobsons Bay Chess Club Inc. Late 2003 Williamstown RSL era begins A stable home for larger events By the end of 2003, Williamstown RSL became the home of chess in the western suburbs. Miles Patterson won the title during this transition. Hobsons Bay Chess Club Inc. Who Can Play?Our Play Chess program is designed for adults and older juniors who want regular, organised chess – from relaxed social games to serious rated tournaments.New or Returning PlayersHaven't played in years? We'll help you ease back into club chess with friendly games and clear guidance.Regular Club PlayersPlay weekly classical or rapid tournaments, improve your rating and test yourself against strong opposition.Casual & Social PlayersPrefer no clocks and no pressure? Join our social nights for relaxed games and conversation.Club Nights - Weekly Competitive ChessHBCC runs regular classical and rapid tournaments on our club nights. These events are structured, paired rounds where you’ll be matched against players of similar strength over multiple weeks. When: Tuesdays from around 7:15pm until late.Format: Classical or rapid events depending on the term.Pairings: Swiss-system pairings managed on our tournament site.Who: Suitable for adults and older juniors comfortable with clocks and notation.Note: For specific time controls and round dates, refer to the Seniors calendar.View Seniors CalendarSocial Nights - Chess Without the PressureSocial nights are relaxed, non-competitive gatherings designed for chess enthusiasts of all skill levels. No clocks, no stress – just friendly games at your own pace.Casual atmosphere – focus on enjoying the game.Open to all levels – perfect for beginners and casual players.Meet fellow enthusiasts and make new friends.Optional tips and guidance from experienced players and coaches.Who can join?Anyone – adults, teens and older juniors. Social nights are ideal if you’re new to club chess.Register for Social NightTournaments & Ratings How It WorksIf you’re new to organised chess, the terminology can be confusing. Here’s a simple guide to the types of events we run and how ratings work. Classical EventsLonger games (for example 60-90 minutes per player) played over several weeks as part of a club championship or seasonal event.Rapid EventsFaster games (for example 10-25 minutes per player), often played as one-day or evening events, ideal for busy players.Swiss System PairingsAfter each round you're paired against someone on a similar score. You're not knocked out ? everyone keeps playing each round.RatingsWe use ratings (club, ACF or FIDE, depending on the event) to help match players fairly and track improvement over time. Links to pairings and standings are usually shared via Tornelo or our tournament pages.How to Get StartedGetting started at HBCC is simple. Follow these steps and we’ll take care of the rest.Step 1 - Choose Your NightDecide whether you want to start with a social night (no clocks) or jump straight into a club tournament.Step 2 - Register or Contact UsFor most tournaments and social nights, you’ll register via our Member & Events portal – links are provided on our Calendar and event pages. If you’re unsure, send us a quick message.Step 3 - Come Along a Bit EarlyArrive 10-15 minutes before the start time so we can say hello, show you around and answer any questions.Step 4 - Bring the EssentialsJust bring yourself and a positive attitude. We provide boards, pieces and clocks. If you know how to keep score, bring a pen.Not sure where to start? Contact us and we’ll recommend the best first session for you. Contact the ClubFrequently Asked QuestionsDo I need to be a member to play? You can often try a session or event before committing to membership, but regular players will be asked to join HBCC. I haven't played in years is that OK? Absolutely. Many of our adult players are returning to chess after a long break. Do I need to know how to use a chess clock and keep score? It helps for tournaments, but we’re happy to show you. Social nights are a great place to learn without pressure. Are there minimum age requirements for club nights? Younger juniors usually start in our Juniors program. Older juniors who are comfortable with clocks may be invited into seniors events – speak with our coaches or committee. How much does it cost? Event and membership fees are kept affordable. Please see our Membership page for current rates. Ready to Play?Join us for a social night or club event and discover why HBCC is the home of chess in Melbourne’s West. View Calendar

Who Is Our Juniors Chess For?HBCC welcomes juniors of all abilities – from absolute beginners to strong tournament players. New to ChessChildren who are learning the moves, rules and basic checkmates.Developing JuniorsKids who know the rules and want to improve tactics, strategy and confidence.Tournament PlayersJuniors already playing in school or club events who want stronger competition and ratings.Future ChampionsHighly motivated juniors aiming for state, national or international pathways.A Clear Pathway from Beginner to Competitive ChessHBCC offers a simple, progressive pathway that supports juniors as they grow from beginners into confident, competitive players.Step 1 - Learn the BasicsRules, piece movement, checkmate patterns and simple tactics.Step 2 - Build SkillsTactics training, openings, endgames and good thinking habits.Step 3 - Compete RegularlyJunior tournaments and internal events to apply learning under time pressure.Step 4 - Aim HigherSupport and guidance for external events and higher-level pathways for advanced juniors.Programs & LevelsWe offer Junior Coaching where we group juniors by experience (not by age) so every child is challenged at the right level in a supportive environment. Beginners GroupPerfect for beginners to start learning the rules of the game and basic skills before learning competitive chess. Intermediate GroupFor juniors who know the rules and want to learn openings, basic tactics, strategy, endgames, tournament readiness and more. Advanced GroupFor our more advanced juniors aiming to compete in higher-level events with advanced tactics, calculation, evaluation, repertoire preparation and much more. One-on-One CoachingPersonalised private lessons for rapid progress — targeted training, game analysis, customised study plan and competition readiness.Weekly Tournament & Coaching ScheduleOur Juniors coaching program runs parallel to school terms. Our Junior tournaments and social nights happen all through the year including school holidays. We aim to provide a safe, welcoming environment for every child.Behaviour & Fair Play:We expect respectful behaviour, good sportsmanship and fair play. Parents and juniors should review our Code of Conduct and club policies.Drop-off & Pick-up:Please arrive on time, sign in if required, and ensure your child is collected promptly after the session ends.Communication: Important updates are shared via email and our club platforms. If you have questions, contact the Juniors Coordinator.Coaching PoliciesHow to EnrolHBCC offers a simple, progressive pathway that supports juniors as they grow from beginners into confident, competitive players.Step 1 - Check the Juniors CalendarSee term dates and upcoming events.Step 2 - Contact usSend us an enquiry here Step 3 - Register online & attend orientationWe will send you the link to register and a link to join a 15 min Zoom call. Step 4 - Come Along to the First SessionArrive a little early so we can welcome your child and answer questions.Enroll NowFrequently Asked QuestionsWhat age can my child start? Most children start from around [X] years old. If your child is younger but keen, contact us to discuss. Does my child need to know the rules already? No. Our Foundation group is designed for absolute beginners. Do I need to stay during the session? Parents of younger children are encouraged to stay; older juniors can be dropped off and picked up on time. See Guidelines & Policiy What does my child need to bring? We provide boards and clocks. A drink bottle is recommended. If your child keeps score, bring a pen. Are there extra costs for tournaments? Some tournaments and special events have separate entry fees, listed on the registration page. How do I know if my child is ready to move up a level? Speak with our coaches or the Juniors Coordinator. We’ll recommend the most suitable group. Over the history of the Hobsons Bay Chess Club, dating back to 1974, there are many people whose contribution we cherish and all would agree that the person with the greatest impact over these years was Peter Caissa. Peter was a long-standing president and junior coach of the club and also a friend and mentor to its members. Sadly, he lost his battle with cancer in 2012. Peterâ€™s contribution to the club goes beyond that of the positions he held. His love of chess was strong, so much so, he changed his surname to Caissa by deed poll. To those that knew him, played with and against him, his passion for the game was infectious The legacy of Peterâ€™s commitment to junior chess and coaching remain strong today. Many now adult players at the club gained the love of the game through Peterâ€™s dedication and owe much to his hard work. Peter said some of his proudest moments was seeing juniors at the club mature by playing chess. Peter was also the driving force behind the annual Best in the West weekend tournament, bringing some of Victoriaâ€™s best chess talent together, along with interstate and international players. The Best in the West tournament had become the biggest chess event in Melbourneâ€™s west and is still going strong today. Away from the Hobsons Bay Chess Club, Peter had terrific success in international correspondence chess events, winning and captaining a number of International Correspondence Federation events. In the 1990s, he helped bring chess to the Melbourne airways through the weekly â€œChess Chatâ€ program. These involvements elevated Peter as a much loved member of the Australian chess community. In 2012, the Hobsons Bay Chess Club took the decision to honour Peter by awarding the Peter Caissa Cup to the winner of the annual club championship. To win the Peter Caissa Cup is no small achievement. Firstly, it requires players to qualify as one of the top eight players during regular season play. The winner is then required to outperform the other seven qualifiers in a round robin club championship event. The words below are a tribute to Peter written by Dallas Gatti, a long time club member and inaugural winner of the Peter Caissa cup.Winning the inaugural Peter Caissa was for me, a huge honour. Peter had not been at the club for quite a while due to his health, but he had planned on being there on presentation night to hand over the cup that was named in his honour. I was looking forward to receive the cup from him, my friend. But the news broke that night, that was not going to happen. I didn’t make a speech that night, my emotions got the better of me. I met Peter Caissa in around 1988, when the club had organised a simul at the Altona Festival. Peter was my first point of contact with the club, and was the first point of contact for many members who joined the club before and after myself. Peter was a great character and stalwart of the club. He would be one of the first people there to help start setting the club up, and one of the last to leave at the end of the evening. He wore many hats, from taking photos and submitting them to local papers to try to increase the clubs recognition, club president, tournament director, arbiter, Winter Inter-club team organiser, and even help organise a chess radio program on local radio. Everything he did, for the club, he did with passion and selflessness. He was a great ambassador for the club. But not only that, he was a great person in life. He was a true friend to most people, and would help you out however he could. Simply, thank you Peter for all that you have done for myself personally during my difficult times in life, and I hope wherever you are, you stop playing the French Defence!!
